clue.text: Domesticated bird

parts.note: a bird that lives around people's homes, read as a tame or home-dwelling bird; the clue runs on into 9 across

explanation.surface: A tame bird kept at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 9 across, where the same bird loses its first part and is put with grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The common small brown bird of towns nests in buildings, hence its name tying it to dwellings.

clue.text: The boss to give me a hand out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of me a hand are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: The boss asked to lend a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on ME A HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A headman is the chief or leader of a village or tribe, so a boss.

clue.text: This the hand to get to win

definitions.text: This the hand to get to win

parts.words: This the hand to get to win
parts.note: the idiom of gaining the advantage: having the better hand in a contest

explanation.surface: Advice on which card hand will win the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the upper hand is to gain control or the advantage over a rival.

clue.text: They keep the reception exclusive

parts.note: reception here is radio or audio signal heard privately by one listener, not a party

explanation.surface: Bouncers keeping a wedding party for invited guests only.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones let only the wearer hear the sound, keeping what is received private.

clue.text: Merry wife in the book of the play

definitions.text: Merry wife in the book of the play

parts.words: Merry wife in the book of the play
parts.note: one of the two title wives in Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor, also a leaf of any book

explanation.surface: Looking up a cheerful wife in a play's script.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Page is one of Shakespeare's merry wives, and a book is made of leaves of that name.

clue.text: Romeo's first love comes right round with description of solution

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a salt solution is described as saline

explanation.surface: Romeo's first sweetheart returns with a chemistry write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Before Juliet, Romeo pines for Rosaline in Shakespeare's play. 'Solution' is a liquid mixture, not an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy, the young man is in love with this woman before he meets Juliet.

clue.text: Picking it was an inside job

definitions.text: Picking it was an inside job

parts.words: Picking it was an inside job
parts.note: an inside job read literally as work done by prisoners inside a jail, unpicking old rope

explanation.surface: A burglary pulled off by someone on the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing apart old tarred rope into loose fibre was traditional hard labour for convicts.

clue.text: Airway in action so took off

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
a duct is a passage for air

explanation.surface: An airline swings into action and the plane departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' suggests a plane departing; here it means subtracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off an amount, as from a bill, is subtracting it.

clue.text: … and what it feels like to touch down

definitions.text: and what it feels like to touch down

parts.words: and what it feels like to touch down
parts.note: down read as soft feathers, so the feel of them to the fingers, not a plane landing

explanation.surface: A pilot describes the sensation of landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft feathers feel light and downy, like a mass of fine fibres.

clue.text: … put to grass when evicted?

parts.note: the bird of 1 across loses its house, and that bird joined to grass gives the old folk name of a vegetable

explanation.surface: A bird turned out of its home and sent out to pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: Continue from 1 across: evict the HOUSE from HOUSE SPARROW, put SPARROW with GRASS, and you have the folk name of the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrowgrass was a common old corruption of the name of this green spear-like vegetable.

clue.text: Sound once heard in Drury Lane

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was an actress at the Theatre Royal in London's Drury Lane in the 1660s

explanation.surface: An echo of old London theatre in a famous street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' points to the 17th century, when Nell Gwyn acted at Drury Lane; the silent K makes the sound of a bell toll match her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow sound of a bell tolling for a death is a knell.

clue.text: Describes terrain extremely handy on a planet

parts.note: Mars is the red planet

indicators.note: extremely takes just the outermost letters of the word handy

explanation.surface: Useful ground conditions found on another world.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy, waterlogged ground is fen-like, an adjective describing land.

clue.text: Pudding a disappointment for Horner

definitions.meaning: a boiled suet pudding with dried fruit
Little Jack Horner pulled out a plum; a bad (duff) one would let him down

explanation.definitionFit: A steamed suet pudding with raisins is a sailor's dessert, and a duff fruit would have spoilt the nursery-rhyme boy's pie.

clue.text: Noddy getting brown in Brazil ?

indicators.note: in puts one word inside another

parts.note: a Brazil is a kind of nut
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: The toy-town character gets a suntan in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy is a children's book character, but here it is an adjective, 'nodding'. 'Brazil' looks like the country; it is the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this word for a flower head that droops or nods.

clue.text: Bell with a bird symbol of the brave

parts.note: Great Tom is a famous bell, at Christ Church, Oxford
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A bell carries a bird emblem for warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: The war axe is linked with Native American warriors, called braves.

clue.text: Chivalrous ? Mrs Mopp was the opposite, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word spoken aloud

parts.note: Mrs Mopp, the charwoman in the radio comedy ITMA, was a daily cleaner, so the opposite is a word for at night

explanation.surface: Was a famous cleaner the reverse of gallant?
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in British English is a cleaning lady; Mrs Mopp of the wartime radio show ITMA was the classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving with the honour and courtesy of a medieval mounted warrior.

clue.text: Fruity source of information

parts.note: the plant bearing fruit for wine, and the informal channel by which rumours spread

explanation.surface: A juicy bit of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the vine is getting it as gossip; literally the plant carries bunches of fruit.

clue.text: Search about before getting most odd result

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a quest is a search
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An investigation turns up a very strange outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' and 'result' only link the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangest and most peculiar, the superlative of an old word for odd.

clue.text: Material for the house was revolutionary.

parts.note: a house is a home
spun means turned round, made revolutions

explanation.surface: Fabric for the household was radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics; here it means rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth woven from yarn made at home, a coarse homemade fabric.

clue.text: Capital for fireside design?

parts.note: a hob is a shelf beside a fireplace
design is art

explanation.surface: A pattern for decorating a fireplace?
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the state capital of Tasmania in Australia.

clue.text: Will in charge of singing

parts.note: William Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: William leads a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to bards, the poets and minstrels who sang verse.

clue.text: Camouflage part of traffic once allowed in

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of the following words

explanation.surface: A disguised portion of vehicles that were once permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across traffiC ONCE ALlowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To camouflage something is to hide it from view.

clue.text: Like Beethoven violently executed?

parts.note: executed violently suggests the guillotine or axe; the composer's name seen with its head chopped off

explanation.surface: A wild performance of a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone executed by the axe has had the head cut off, and the composer's name shorn of its first letter is the same idea.

clue.text: Tired of wrestling

definitions.meaning: a freestyle style of wrestling with few rules

explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out is an informal sense, and freestyle wrestling is so called.

clue.text: Exercise after some divestment

definitions.meaning: a piece of work set for learning
after taking off clothes you have fewer on

explanation.definitionFit: A class or school exercise, and the phrase read as wearing fewer clothes.

clue.text: Brief look over the West End

parts.note: to scan is to look over

indicators.note: End picks the final letter of the word West

explanation.surface: A quick glance round London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district; 'End' takes the last letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre and in short supply, as in scant attention.

clue.text: In this place in, Paris instead

definitions.text: In this place in, Paris instead

parts.words: In this place in, Paris instead
parts.note: the French word for place, which preceded by in gives the English idiom meaning instead

explanation.surface: Visiting Paris rather than somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: The French noun for a place, used in English after 'in' to mean in place of.

clue.text: Sort of lower gear to encourage horse-power

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the letters of lower are rearranged

explanation.surface: Engaging a lower gear for extra engine power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse-power' and 'gear' suggest a car; the gear is riding tack.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiked wheel on a rider's spur, used to urge the horse on.

clue.text: Put out by the heat.

parts.note: knocked out of a competition in a qualifying round, not bothered by hot weather

explanation.surface: Feeling bothered in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knocked out in a qualifying round of a race is to be removed from the competition.

clue.text: Odd how it runs in the mind serving as an agent

indicators.note: odd how suggests the letters of it runs come out strangely jumbled

parts.note: mental means in the mind

explanation.surface: A remark on how strangely thoughts run through one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the means by which something is done, as an instrument or agent is.
